findings.title: Findings converge on HassetteActionPayload construction at receive time
findings.why_it_matters: D3 makes `HassetteActionPayload(name, data={})` the place a `hassette_action` message is validated: it is built by `construct_ignoring_unknown_keys` inside `create_event_from_hass`, before any listener sees the event. Three findings from both critics land on that one step from different sides. A missing `name` drops the event with a log line that names neither the event type nor the field (Finding 2). The drop hits every subscriber, wildcard ones included, while wrong-typed `name`/`data` construct fine because a dataclass checks nothing (Finding 3). The `{}` default covers only a missing `data` key, not `data: null` or a non-mapping (Finding 4). Each proposes its own patch: a richer dispatch log, a tolerant payload, a normalization in the factory. Does this point to a problem with where envelope validation lives, rather than three gaps to fix one by one? The re-evaluation is open-ended: whether receive-time validation of this envelope is needed at all, which failures belong to receive time versus the per-handler filter and extractor, and whether some of these are limitations to accept and document.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate `HassetteActionPayload` construction at receive time before addressing Findings 2, 3 and 4 individually. Open questions: should a malformed envelope be dropped before delivery or delivered and failed per handler; what does "loud" mean for a dropped event; which shapes (missing `name`, `data: null`, non-mapping `data`, wrong types) does the payload own versus the filter and extractor.
findings.chosen: B: Keep receive-time construction as D3 ratified it and address Findings 2, 3 and 4 individually.
findings.choice_reason: Recommendation changed in session: D3 already ratified the drop; the new facts are a log gap and a dev-only path

findings.title: A dropped hassette_action logs neither the event type nor the missing field
findings.why_it_matters: The Posture promises a logged error "that names the field", and D3 promises a malformed message "fails loudly at receive time". The real path for a missing `name` is `cls(**data)` raising `TypeError` -> `WebsocketIO.dispatch` -> `log_dispatch_failure`, which deliberately logs only `command_label(data)` (`'event' (id N)`), the exception type and traceback frames, never `str(exc)`. The log reads "Failed to dispatch message 'event' (id 812): TypeError" plus frames: no `hassette_action`, no `name`. The user's automation silently never fires and the log doesn't say which event or field. The dropped event also never reaches wildcard `hass.event.*` listeners, which the ledger doesn't state.
findings.recommended: B: Keep receive-time construction and make the dispatch failure log name the HA `event_type` and the missing or unexpected key names (never values).
findings.chosen: B: Keep receive-time construction and make the dispatch failure log name the HA `event_type` and the missing or unexpected key names (never values).

findings.title: A malformed hand-fired event is lost to every subscriber, while wrong-typed fields pass construction
findings.why_it_matters: Today a hand-fired `hassette_action` without `name` still reaches generic `hass.event.*` listeners (loggers, recorders, user `bus.on(topic=...)` predicates). After D3, construction raises inside `create_event_from_hass` and the event is dropped for all consumers, not just the typed handler. Meanwhile the dataclass checks no types: `name: 5` or `data: "x"` construct fine; the `name` filter then silently never matches and `D.HassetteActionData` fails later with a conversion error. So "fails loudly at receive time" covers only a missing `name`, not wrong types. The Posture's "loud failure" was written about handler failure, not "the event vanishes for every other subscriber".
findings.recommended: B: Keep strict construction and add to D3's ratified sentence that a malformed event is withheld from every subscriber and that wrong-typed `name`/`data` are not caught at receive time.
findings.chosen: B: Keep strict construction and add to D3's ratified sentence that a malformed event is withheld from every subscriber and that wrong-typed `name`/`data` are not caught at receive time.

findings.title: D3's `{}` default covers only a missing `data` key, not `data: null` or a non-mapping
findings.why_it_matters: D3 says the payload default "settles missing `data`". The dataclass default applies only when the key is absent; `create_event_from_hass`'s `or {}` normalizes only the outer event data. A hand-fired event with `data:` and no value (YAML null) builds `payload.data.data = None`, and `ensure_present` skips every `D.HassetteActionData` handler with "returned NoneType, expected a value". A string or list `data` constructs fine and fails at extraction with a generic converter message. Both are logged per handler, so not silent, but D3's claim is broader than the behavior. A related unstated test surface: `dict | Model` annotations are short-circuited by `TYPE_MATCHER.matches` and never reach the new D1 branch.
findings.recommended: B: Narrow D3's wording: a missing `data` defaults to `{}`; `data: null` or a non-mapping fails per handler at extraction. Add `data: null`, `Model | None` and `dict | Model` as stated test cases.
findings.chosen: B: Narrow D3's wording: a missing `data` defaults to `{}`; `data: null` or a non-mapping fails per handler at extraction. Add `data: null`, `Model | None` and `dict | Model` as stated test cases.

findings.title: The ratified payload signature `data: dict[str, Any] = {}` can't be a dataclass default
findings.why_it_matters: `@dataclass` rejects a mutable default at class definition (`ValueError: mutable default <class 'dict'> for field data is not allowed: use default_factory`), so building from the ledger's text breaks import of the whole events package. Separately, `frozen=True` doesn't freeze the dict: one dict instance is handed to every handler of the event, so one handler's mutation is visible to its siblings. Existing payloads share that property, so the second point is consistent with the house style, not a regression.
findings.chosen: In D3's criteria table header and **Ratified:** sentence, write the payload as `HassetteActionPayload(name: str, data: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict))`. No other change; the shared-dict note matches existing payloads and needs no fix.

findings.title: pydantic's ValidationError text carries `input_value`, which reaches logs and execution records
findings.why_it_matters: `ParameterInjector.convert_value` embeds `{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}` in the `DependencyResolutionError` message, and `track_execution` stores `str(exc)` as the execution record's `error_message`, which the monitoring UI and DB keep. A pydantic v2 `ValidationError` string includes `input_value=...` for each failing field, so D1 routes user message payloads (room names, free text) into logs and telemetry. The inbound WebSocket module explicitly forbids this ("exception messages ... can quote those values (e.g. a pydantic `input_value`)"). Note the DI conversion path already quotes values today (`Unable to convert {value!r} ...` in `TYPE_REGISTRY` and the union branch), so D1 extends an existing inconsistency rather than starting one. Audience assumption: personal data in a solo user's own logs is mostly harmless; it matters because this is an open-source library whose users paste logs into issues.
findings.recommended: A: In the D1 branch, catch `ValidationError` and re-raise `UnableToConvertValueError` from `errors(include_input=False)`, naming locations and messages only.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as consistent with how DI conversion errors already quote values.

findings.title: For `Model | None`, the union branch replaces the field-naming error with a useless one
findings.why_it_matters: The union branch tries each arm and raises `UnableToConvertValueError(f"Unable to convert {value!r} to {tp!r}") from last_err`. The injector's message includes only that outer exception's text, so the model arm's pydantic error, the one that names the field, never appears; with `Model | None` the chained cause is the `NoneType` arm's "Cannot convert ... to NoneType" anyway. The "names the field" promise fails for the most natural way to make a model parameter optional.
findings.chosen: Add to D1's **Calls made during the build** (or a note under D1): when every union arm fails, the raised message includes the error text of each non-`NoneType` arm (sanitized per Finding 6's outcome), not just a chained final-arm cause. Add `Model | None` and `dict | Model` to D1's tests.

findings.title: D1 builds a new `TypeAdapter` on every conversion
findings.why_it_matters: D1's mechanism is `pydantic.TypeAdapter(tp).validate_python`, with no mention of reuse. Constructing a `TypeAdapter` builds a core schema; for a `BaseModel` it reuses the model's schema, but for a stdlib dataclass it is rebuilt each time. The branch fires for any Mapping value with a model or dataclass annotation on any custom event, so a busy custom event pays it on every dispatch. `state_changed` handlers are unaffected (the `BaseState` branch comes first).
findings.recommended: A: Use `tp.model_validate` for `BaseModel` targets and a `functools.cache`d `TypeAdapter` factory for dataclass targets.
findings.chosen: A: Use `tp.model_validate` for `BaseModel` targets and a `functools.cache`d `TypeAdapter` factory for dataclass targets.

findings.title: The ledger's Homes list misses registration points, including the codegen source of the sync mirror
findings.why_it_matters: The Homes list names `src/hassette/bus/sync_events.py` as the sync mirror's home, but that file is generated ("Do not edit this file directly"); the mirror comes from `BUS_EVENT_SHORTCUTS` in codegen. Other sites that enumerate `on_component_loaded`/`ComponentLoadedEvent` are also absent: the forgotten-await completeness test, the harness coverage table, the docs xref map, the `hassette.events` exports, and the troubleshooting page's `on_*` list. `D.EventData`'s docstring ("Use with `Bus.emit`") goes stale once D1 makes it work for HA events.
findings.chosen: In the Summary's Homes list, replace "plus its sync mirror in `src/hassette/bus/sync_events.py`" with "plus `on_hassette_action` in `BUS_EVENT_SHORTCUTS` (`codegen/src/hassette_codegen/sync_facade/generic.py`), which regenerates `src/hassette/bus/sync_events.py`", and add a bullet: "Registration lists: `tests/unit/test_forgotten_await_completeness.py`, `tests/unit/test_harness_coverage.py`, `tools/docs/check_xref_coverage.py`, `src/hassette/events/__init__.py` exports, `docs/pages/troubleshooting.md`'s `on_*` list, and `D.EventData`'s docstring (D1 makes it work beyond `Bus.emit`)."

findings.title: The filter parameter `action` matches the `name` field and collides with HA's own meaning of "action"
findings.why_it_matters: `on_hassette_action(action="tracker_done")` filters on the payload's `name`, and `simulate_hassette_action(action, ...)` sets it. In Home Assistant, "action" is the service being called (here always `hassette.send`); hass-hassette's README and hautomate call the thing a message with a name (`ha_messages`, `*_MESSAGE`, `MessageData`, `named()`). A reader sees `action=` and maps it to the HA action, not to `name`. The ledger chose `action` only because `name=` is taken by the listener-name keyword; it never weighed an alternative. The house convention names the filter after the field it matches (`component`, `domain`/`service`), which is impossible here.
findings.recommended: B: Rename the filter and harness parameter to `message` (`on_hassette_action("tracker_done", ...)` unchanged positionally; keyword becomes `message=`).
findings.chosen: Rename the whole concept to "message" end to end: hass-hassette event type hassette_message, on_hassette_message(message=), D.MessageData, simulate_hassette_message
findings.choice_reason: User asked to consider names from first principles, including the method name; chose message family over send/command/action

findings.title: Lax validation silently ignores mistyped keys when the model field has a default
findings.why_it_matters: D1's ratification accepts pydantic lax mode (`"5"` -> `5`), but not the companion behavior: pydantic models and dataclasses ignore extra keys by default. A dashboard sending `romm: kitchen` to a model with `room: str = "living"` validates "successfully" and the handler runs with the default. D1 makes this the framework-wide behavior for every Mapping -> model conversion. hautomate's converter behaves the same, so it's no regression there.
findings.recommended: A: Add a sentence to D1's ratified trade-off and to `docs/pages/core-concepts/bus/dependency-injection.md`: extra keys are ignored; set `extra="forbid"` (models) or the dataclass config equivalent to fail on stray keys.
findings.chosen: A: Add a sentence to D1's ratified trade-off and to `docs/pages/core-concepts/bus/dependency-injection.md`: extra keys are ignored; set `extra="forbid"` (models) or the dataclass config equivalent to fail on stray keys.

findings.title: The hass-hassette <-> hassette coupling has no version floor and no system test
findings.why_it_matters: After D3, hass-hassette's README example (`event.payload.data["name"]`) raises `TypeError: 'HassetteActionPayload' object is not subscriptable` on new hassette and works only on old; the updated README will break users on older hassette. Neither repo states a minimum version. The system tests run a pinned hass-hassette, but no test fires `hassette.send` and asserts a `HassetteActionEvent` arrives, so a hass-hassette rename of `name`/`data` or a new required field would surface only as the dispatch-drop log line from Finding 2. The ledger also doesn't list the hass-hassette README change as its own step, though that repo requires a PR.
findings.recommended: A: Add Build items: a system test that calls `hassette.send` and asserts a `HassetteActionEvent` with typed `name`/`data`; a "requires hassette >= X" line in the hass-hassette README update; and the hass-hassette README change as its own PR step.
findings.chosen: A: Add Build items: a system test that calls `hassette.send` and asserts a `HassetteActionEvent` with typed `name`/`data`; a "requires hassette >= X" line in the hass-hassette README update; and the hass-hassette README change as its own PR step.

findings.title: hautomate keeps a duplicate of the new API with no migration step
findings.why_it_matters: hautomate's `ha_messages.py` (`TOPIC`, `named()`, `MessageData[T]` with its own `TypeAdapter` converter) duplicates what this design adds. Its callers keep working after D3 (`get_path` reads attributes; an already-converted value short-circuits D1), so nothing breaks, but the duplicate becomes a second source of truth for the same contract. The ledger has no follow-up to retire it. On the other side, hautomate is a separate repo, and this design's scope is hassette.
findings.recommended: A: Add a line under Build: after release, hautomate replaces `ha_messages.py` with `on_hassette_action` and `D.HassetteActionData`.
findings.chosen: B: Leave hautomate out of the ledger.
